problems.title: Build against the nsiccha/flatppl-rust dogfood compiler line
problems.summary: flatppl-python-api is pinned to the dogfood branch of the nsiccha/flatppl-rust fork, which merges upstream flatppl-rust main and adds the compiler fixes the Python fixes here rely on (corrcholesky(n), odesolve, nested product charts, regression reductions for data on reals, packed fixed data, odesolve gradients that exclude the step-size controller, eigh and svd vector derivatives at a zero off-diagonal entry, real symmetric eigh lowered to the helper an analytic enzyme-ad rule differentiates, and opt-in sensitivity error control for odesolve gradients). Cargo.lock is regenerated by cargo.

fix.why_together: The pin and its re-pins: Cargo.toml and the Cargo.lock cargo writes for it, with the changelog entries and regression tests of what a re-pin fixes.

validation.detail: Full flatppl-python test suite on the line after the merge of upstream main 1b914f2, with the extension built --locked against nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53 and enzyme-ad installed from the declared URL, jax 0.12.0.1, x86_64 Linux, Python 3.14 with 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.batchedreverse.1: 633 passed, 0 failed (run at fef8682; the tip adds only a changelog edit). Python 3.13 with the 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.1 wheel the other 11 targets declare was not rerun on this tip; its last full run, at e67cb4d with the compiler at 6ea3e13, gave 621 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped.

The test passes with the pin and fails with nsiccha/flatppl-rust b1fe90f, where forward and reverse derivatives at the diagonal matrix are exactly 0 against -0.0775. Forward and reverse directional derivatives of a sign-invariant function of the eigh vectors (sum_i c_i (w . v_i)^2) along a symmetric direction match JAX's own eigh to rtol 1e-10 at diagonal(1, 2, 3.5, 5) and at a nearby generic symmetric matrix. Real symmetric eigh and eigvalsh lower to the __enzyme_linalg_eigh_v1_* helper: with the declared CPython 3.14 Linux x86_64 wheel, whose analytic rule differentiates it, a 30 by 30 value and gradient under jax.jit on one CPU takes 0.42 ms (eigh vectors) and 0.59 ms (eigvalsh) on nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53, instead of 33 and 39 ms with the alpha 23 wheel, which differentiates the Jacobi iteration; gradients within 2.7e-13 (analytic rule) and 8.2e-13 (alpha 23) of JAX's eigh, values identical. With the compiler at 6ea3e13 the same measurement gave about 3.5 and 175 ms.

problems.title: Module.logdensity and generated queries refused corrcholesky(n) parameters
problems.summary: The compiler reports the support of LKJCholesky(n, eta) as {"set": "corrcholesky", "n": n}. The package wrote it as a bare `corrcholesky`, so log densities over such parameters failed to infer, LogDensity bounds raised "no element bounds for the set 'corrcholesky'", and an unbound extent was not reported (PosteriorDB dogs-dogs_nonhierarchical, sat-hier_2pl, synthetic_grid_RBF_kernels-kronecker_gp).

fix.why_together: The set's text, bounds and extent check with their tests, and a faster Stan reference for the 30 x 30 test.

validation.detail: 5 tests passed; each fails on the unmodified package. LKJ priors of PosteriorDB dogs-dogs_nonhierarchical, sat-hier_2pl (n = 2) and synthetic_grid_RBF_kernels-kronecker_gp (n = 30, 435 coordinates): Module.logdensity values within 7.6e-15 and directional derivatives within 2.6e-15 relative of a 50-digit evaluation of Stan's chart and lkj_corr_cholesky_lpdf; within 2.9e-13 (value) and 3.2e-12 (gradient) of BridgeStan 2.9.0 where Stan's double arithmetic is accurate (smallest diagonal at least 1e-3); identical to compile_transformed. Rechecked on nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53 with the declared wheel.

problems.title: LogDensity.grad and potential fail to stage queries with runtime checks
problems.summary: Module.logdensity jitted grad and potential with plain jax.jit. For a query whose compiled module reports runtime checks (a singular linear solve, an index range), the first call failed with "Cannot abstractly evaluate a checkify.check which was not functionalized", although calling fn eagerly worked. They now functionalize the checks and raise a failed check after the call.

fix.why_together: One change to the staging in Module.logdensity, with its test.

validation.detail: The test passes; with the previous plain jax.jit staging it fails with the reported 'not functionalized' error.

problems.title: Compiled queries over fixed data repeated their likelihood setup on every call
problems.summary: With fixed data, a reduced likelihood such as a Gaussian regression over loaded bounded rows emitted the setup of its data-only summaries, a bounded QR with its loops and linear-solve check, into the scoring program, and XLA does not fold loops over constants. Module now exports with prepare_fixed_data, runs the compiler's preparation once per compile, checks its status, and passes its outputs after the declared inputs of every call. Upstream fixed it in #156 (prepare_fixed_data, summaries shared per data binding and device, the inline score when a preparation check fails); since the merge of upstream main 1b914f2 the line runs upstream's implementation and tests.

fix.why_together: One change to how Module exports and CompiledFunction calls a query, with its tests, type stub and changelog entry.

validation.detail: Since the merge of upstream main 1b914f2 the line runs upstream's implementation and upstream's tests/test_fixed_data_preparation.py, whose 10 tests pass on nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53: a fixed Gaussian regression's QR leaves the per-call scores, gradients and batches (float32 and float64); the first compile under jit prepares once per data snapshot; the prepared parameter check follows the score policy; a score compiled on a concrete mesh runs on another device; logdensity keeps the inline option; a failing fixed-data check (a value outside its declared set, an index out of range) keeps the inline score policy instead of raising at compile; promoted literal observations stay live; rebinding external observations prepares the new values. The per-call timings measured for the fork's own implementation were not repeated for upstream's.

problems.title: Gaussian regressions over fixed data declared on reals kept the full likelihood
problems.summary: Only regressions whose loaded rows declared bounded entries reduced to prepared summaries; data declared on reals or posreals, as PosteriorDB writes earnings-earn_height and nes1984-nes, and data bound with Module.set scored the full likelihood on every call. With the compiler pin that proves such data finite from their values, they are prepared once per compile like bounded rows. The test that expected no preparation for set-bound data on reals now checks that loaded and bound data on reals are prepared. The compiler side is upstream flatppl-rust #753; upstream flatppl-python pins a compiler without it.

fix.why_together: The tests and changelog entry for the reduction the pinned compiler adds; the Python code path is the fixed-data preparation.

validation.detail: The test, rewritten against upstream's preparation API in the merge, passes on nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53: loaded rows declared on reals and rows bound with Module.set on reals are prepared (CompiledFunction.preparation_stablehlo is set), the per-call program has no stablehlo.while, and values and gradients match the closed form (1e-12 / 1e-11), and values match the programs compiled with prepare_fixed_data=False and with sufficient_statistics=False (1e-13). Its earlier form failed with the compiler at 87ebd09 (no preparation); the rewritten form was not run against a compiler without the reduction. Since ef74f53 the compiler reduces such data only for a prepared compile, as upstream's compiler does for bounded data. Measured before the merge: on PosteriorDB earnings-earn_height with its data declared on reals, compile_transformed(logdensity=True) held the same three prepared summaries as a bounded copy of the query; over 60 points values and gradients agreed with prepare_fixed_data=False to 1.9e-14 and 4.0e-13 relative, and with a 50-digit evaluation to 2.8e-14 and 3.1e-13. Data declared on posreals reduce too.

problems.title: Reverse-mode gradients through odesolve failed: enzyme-ad refused data-dependent while loops
problems.summary: odesolve lowers to an adaptive Dormand-Prince loop whose trip count depends on the parameters. The declared alpha 23 enzyme-ad wheels refuse to reverse such a stablehlo.while ("WhileOp does not have known iteration count for cache removal"), so LogDensity.grad failed on any odesolve model. The CPython 3.14 Linux x86_64 dependency line now names the flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.3 pre-release wheel of nsiccha/Enzyme-JAX by exact URL and sha256. The other targets' wheels followed in enzyme-ad-every-target.

fix.why_together: The dependency declaration, its changelog entry and the test that needs it.

requires.name: enzyme-ad 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.3 (cp314 manylinux_2_28 x86_64)
requires.why: Source of the declared wheel, release flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.3, sha256 6e1bc40c48f6d13cf3d3e8978a6d4255094ae4db39e881dae6ce55bb20d57597.

validation.detail: 3 tests passed with the declared wheel, now 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.batchedreverse.1, which keeps the adaptive-while reverse mode; all 3 fail with the alpha 23 wheel ('WhileOp does not have known iteration count for cache removal'). On exponential decay the reverse gradient matches the exact solution to 1e-7 and Enzyme forward mode to 1e-10. On a Lotka-Volterra posterior (rtol 1e-10) reverse-mode gradients agree with forward mode to 1.2e-13 and with an independent sensitivity (scipy DOP853 at 1e-13) to 8.1e-10 away from the steady state; at the exact steady state they are finite but still inaccurate. Rechecked on nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53 in the full suite.

problems.title: value_and_grad returned (-inf, 0) for densities comparing a Boolean array with an integer
problems.summary: FlatPPL lowers z .== 1 on a Boolean z to a conversion followed by a comparison. The declared enzyme-ad wheels folded that comparison to false under differentiation, so jax.value_and_grad of such a density returned (-inf, 0) while the plain value was right. The CPython 3.14 Linux x86_64 dependency line now names the flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.1 pre-release wheel of nsiccha/Enzyme-JAX by exact URL and sha256. It keeps adaptive-while reverse mode and adds the comparison fix, an analytic derivative for the compiler's real symmetric eigh helper and imported modules in Enzyme's own dialect. The other targets' wheels followed in enzyme-ad-every-target.

fix.why_together: The dependency declaration, its changelog entry and the test that needs it.

requires.name: enzyme-ad 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.1 (cp314 manylinux_2_28 x86_64)
requires.why: Source of the declared wheel, release flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.1, sha256 1a940ab11001f25127cf2fdd4057785105266d992c1b56b8d36b382e0125ddda.

validation.detail: 2 tests passed with the declared wheel (since 4e37833 the batchedreverse.1 build of the same line): a two-animal Bernoulli posterior written with z .== 1 and with boolean.(z) gives log(0.125) and gradient 2 under jit and value_and_grad. With the alpha 23 wheel and with adaptivewhile.3, the z .== 1 form gives -inf under value_and_grad while the plain value is right. Rechecked on nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53 in the full suite.

problems.title: odesolve gradients missed Stan's, by orders of magnitude at a steady state
problems.summary: odesolve's gradient differentiated the value-only Dormand-Prince steps, whose error control ignores the sensitivities, so it could miss Stan's gradient by more than the solver tolerance, and at an exact steady state (where the error estimate vanishes and the steps grow to the output times) by orders of magnitude. Module.compile, compile_transformed and logdensity take ode_sensitivity_control=True, passed to the compiler's export, which then differentiates a second solve whose step-size control includes the sensitivities, as Stan's coupled system does; values still come from the value-only steps. Off by default: it costs about four times as long on a two-state Lotka-Volterra density and needs an enzyme-ad wheel that loads Enzyme's MLIR dialect. The CPython 3.14 Linux x86_64 dependency line now names the flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.batchedreverse.1 pre-release of nsiccha/Enzyme-JAX, whose batched forward derivatives through reverse the coupled solve needs; the other targets keep alpha 23 and the tests are skipped there. A query that draws random values keeps its draws and successor keys with the option.

fix.why_together: The keyword with its tests and changelog entry, and the dependency declaration whose wheel the option's coupled solve needs.

requires.name: FlatPPL Rust compiler line
requires.why: Emits the coupled sensitivity solve and takes the ode_sensitivity_control keyword on the native export.

requires.name: enzyme-ad 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.batchedreverse.1 (cp314 manylinux_2_28 x86_64)
requires.why: Source of the declared wheel, release flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.enzymedialect.batchedreverse.1, sha256 18d77788ef4bd611aecf85c1b041de70aaa18c0a40943e775bc721c18ff9ca4b.

validation.detail: 10 tests passed with the declared wheel. Exponential decay: the reverse gradient matches the exact solution to 1e-7 with ode_sensitivity_control off and on. Lotka-Volterra at its steady state (all rates 1, initial state (1, 1), rtol 1e-10), where the sensitivities have a closed form (rotations exp(Jt) for the initial state): with the option the reverse gradient matches it to 1.4e-10 relative and equals forward mode to 1e-12; without it the gradient is 4.0e-2 off. Values are bit-identical with and without the option, and a query that solves an ODE and then draws keeps its draw and successor key (the compiler at d111b50 panicked there). One jitted call on one CPU: value and gradient 145 instead of 38 us, value alone 43 instead of 10.7 us. Rechecked on nsiccha/flatppl-rust ef74f53 in the full suite.

problems.title: odesolve and Boolean-comparison gradients failed on every target but CPython 3.14 Linux x86_64
problems.summary: The adaptive-while and Boolean-comparison fixes reached only CPython 3.14 on Linux x86_64, the one target with a fixed enzyme-ad wheel. The other 11 targets (CPython 3.12 to 3.15 on manylinux_2_28 x86_64 and aarch64 and on macOS 14 arm64) kept alpha 23, so LogDensity.grad through odesolve failed there ("WhileOp does not have known iteration count for cache removal") and value_and_grad of a z .== 1 density returned (-inf, 0). Their dependency lines now name the flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.1 pre-release wheels of nsiccha/Enzyme-JAX by exact URL and sha256: alpha 23 plus adaptive-while reverse mode, the comparison fix and the analytic eigh rule, each tested on its own platform before upload. CPython 3.14 Linux x86_64 keeps its newer wheel, the only one that loads Enzyme's dialect, so the ode_sensitivity_control tests stay limited to it; the other gradient tests now run on every target.

fix.why_together: The eleven dependency lines, their changelog entries and the test gates that follow them.

requires.name: enzyme-ad 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.1 (11 wheels: cp312-cp315 manylinux_2_28 aarch64 and macosx_14_0 arm64, cp312/cp313/cp315 manylinux_2_28 x86_64)
requires.why: Source of the declared wheels, release flatppl-alpha.23-adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.1; each wheel's sha256 is on its dependency line and in the release's SHA256SUMS.

validation.detail: Python 3.13 on x86_64 Linux, extension built --locked against nsiccha/flatppl-rust 6ea3e13: with the declared 0.0.15+flatppl.23.adaptivewhile.boolrange.eigh.1 wheel the full suite gives 621 passed, 0 failed, 7 skipped (the ode_sensitivity_control tests, which need Enzyme's dialect; that wheel refuses such a program with an MLIR parse error). With the alpha 23 wheel the same target declared before, the three default-mode odesolve gradient tests fail ('WhileOp does not have known iteration count for cache removal') and the z .== 1 Boolean-comparison test fails, while boolean.(z) passes. A 30 by 30 eigh vector objective and eigvalsh, value and gradient under jax.jit on one CPU: 3.7 and 4.4 ms instead of 217 and 231 ms with alpha 23, gradients within 3.0e-13 of JAX's eigh. Each of the 11 wheels downloaded anonymously matches the release's SHA256SUMS. On Python 3.14 with its unchanged wheel the two changed test files run all 12 tests and pass.
